To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

two ecdysone-regulated genes, BR-C and E74 are expressed selectively in the Kenyon cells of mushroom body in the brain of adult honeybee and that BR-C and another gene, E75, are expressed preferentially at the late stage of oogenesis in the follicle cell of queen honeybee.
two ecdysone-regulated genes, BR-C and E74, were expressed in specific subtypes of Kenyon cells, which are the mushroom body neurons in the brain of adult honeybees.

the ecdysteroid regulated gene Mblk-1 is expressed selectively in Kenyan cell subtypes in mushroom bodies of the worker brain, and that the ecdysteoid regulated genes BR-C and E-75 are expressed selectively in the follicle cell surrounding the egg cells at the later stage of the ovary.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of ecdysone-regulated genes in the adult honey bee.
the role of ecdysteroids in the regulation of gene expression in the brain and ovaries of adult worker honeybees (Apis mellifere).
the molecular mechanisms of ecdysone signaling in the brain, and its role in the control of behavior and reproductive physiology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ecdysteroids are involved in the control of the expression of a number of genes, including the ones that are involved in the development of adult structures, in the adult honeybees.
the expression of these genes is regulated by ecdysteroids, which are involved in both the regulation of brain functions and in the regulation of oogenesis.

the BR-C and E74 genes are expressed in the mushroom bodies, and that BR-C and the E75 genes are expressed in follicle cells of the ovary, and that the expression of BR-C and E93 in mushroom bodies is ecdysteroid-dependent, and that the E74 gene is not ecdysteroid dependent in the honeybee.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

ecdysteroid regulates the expression of several transcriptional factors that have been implicated in the development of various organs, including the brain, in insects, and that these genes are involved in brain functions in the adult honeybees.
the honeybee brain has a sophisticated system to respond to the ecdysteroid signal, which may have a significant impact on the brain function and behavior.
the honeybee brain is a useful model to study the molecular mechanism underlying the ecdysteroid regulation of insect behavior.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ecdysteroid regulates a variety of genes that are differentially expressed in different cell types in the honeybee.
ecdysteroid hormones play a critical role in regulating brain function as well in reproductive physiology in adult honeybees.
we have identified two new ecdysteroid regulated genes that are involved in the control of brain function as in the control of reproductive physiology.
